tagline.text: Sierra Madre forest road and the memorial to Aurora Quezon

location.label: Location
location.text: Aurora–Nueva Ecija border, along the Baler–Bongabon Road

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱300–1,500 (including transport and snacks, per day)

children.text: Aurora Memorial National Park is a protected area of about 5,676 hectares that flanks the road linking Baler and Bongabon across the Sierra Madre ridge. It combines dense lowland forest, birdwatching and the site of the 1949 ambush of Aurora Quezon's party in one mountain drive.

Aurora Memorial National Park is a protected area in the Sierra Madre range on eastern Luzon, straddling the border of Nueva Ecija and Aurora provinces. It covers about 5,676 hectares and stretches more than 50 km along the road that connects Baler and Bongabon. It is managed by the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) and falls under IUCN Category V (protected landscape). In other words, it is not a theme-park-style park with a ticket gate at the entrance, but a scenic park where you drive along the road and take in the forest and ridgelines.

The park's history goes back to 1937, when President Manuel Quezon declared the Bongabon–Baler National Park through Proclamation No. 220, with an initial area of about 2,356 hectares. By 1941 it had grown to its present size. In May 1949 it was dedicated under its current name in honor of Aurora Aragon Quezon, the wife of President Quezon. Doña Aurora was killed on 28 April 1949 on this very mountain road in an ambush by armed men, together with her daughter Maria Aurora and the mayor of Quezon City. So the place is a beautiful forest and, at the same time, a painful site in modern Philippine history.

Most of the forest is lowland dipterocarp, with some montane forest at higher elevations. The maximum altitude is reported to be about 1,000 m. BirdLife International has designated it an Important Bird Area (IBA), and species recorded here include the Philippine duck, spotted imperial-pigeon, flame-breasted fruit-dove, Philippine eagle, Philippine hawk-eagle, green racket-tail, whiskered pitta and Luzon water redstart. If you enjoy birds, walking slowly along the roadside forest in the early morning is a good way to spend time here.

There are a few things to know in advance. The park does not appear to have maintained hiking trails, a large visitor center or clear visitor facilities, and shops inside the park are said to be very few. We also could not find an official entrance fee or opening hours for the park itself. This guide therefore assumes a half-day to full-day trip starting from Baler or Cabanatuan, driving the mountain road and visiting the forest and the memorial site.

The heart of the park is the paved road over the Sierra Madre. It is winding, with many ups and downs and some narrow stretches. Around sunrise or after the rain clears, mist hangs over the ridges and the scenery is especially good.

blocks.title: Aurora Quezon ambush site and memorial marker

children.text: The ambush of Aurora Quezon's party on 28 April 1949 is said to have taken place by the roadside in the Labi area of Bongabon, near KM 168–169. A historical marker stands at the site and was reportedly rededicated on 28 April 2013. Check the exact location of the marker locally.

Tall dipterocarp trees, orchids and ferns line both sides of the road. It is a good place for short walks into the roadside forest and for photos. Since the journey is long, it works better to stop at several points rather than stay long in one place.

Because the area is designated an Important Bird Area, birders like to visit in the early morning. Bring binoculars and walk slowly along the roadside when traffic is light to hear birdsong. The Philippine eagle is extremely rare and is said to be hard to see.
Ditumabo Falls (Mother Falls) in San Luis, close to the park road, is a popular add-on from the Baler side. The walk is about
1.3km
from where vehicles stop, and a guide is required. It is not inside the park, so plan it as a separate outing.

On the park's western side lies the Maria Aurora area, where the Villa Aurora Ecotourism Area and a few lodgings and eateries are found. It is a good base for resting before or after the mountain drive. Check whether places are open before you visit.

items.title: Half day from Baler
items.subtitle: Mountain road drive and memorial site

children.text: Have breakfast in Baler and stock up on water and snacks. There are almost no shops inside the park, so this is the time to prepare.
Head west up the Baler–Bongabon Road. Early in the morning there is little traffic and plenty of birdsong in the forest. Stop briefly at open viewpoints for photos.
Walk briefly along the forest edge by the road and look for birds. There are no maintained trails, so do not go far from the road.
Look for the memorial marker for the ambush of Aurora Quezon in the Labi area of Bongabon and pause for a moment of silence. Check the marker's location and condition locally.
Have lunch in Maria Aurora or toward Cabanatuan, and return your vehicle or transfer if needed.
In the rainy season, fog and rain often reduce visibility even in the daytime, so start early and get out of the mountain section before dark.
Leave Baler and first explore the mountain road section.
Head back, then register at the entrance to Ditumabo Falls in San Luis and hire a guide.
From the point where vehicles cannot go further, walk about
1.3km
to the falls. You will cross a river and pass rocky sections, so wear shoes that can get wet.
Return to Baler for lunch and a rest. It is safer to avoid the falls right after rain.
Seeing both places in one day involves a lot of travel, so consider your stamina and sunset time, and feel free to cut one of them.
Genesis and JoyBus run buses from Manila (Cubao) to Baler. According to 2025 guides, a regular air-conditioned bus costs about
and JoyBus Deluxe or Executive about
The trip is reported to take about
5–7 hours
depending on traffic and mountain road conditions. The route passes over the mountain road on the Bongabon side, so you can see the park section from the bus window.
Departures tend to cluster late at night or in the early morning, so check the latest timetable with the operator.
Staying in Baler makes it easy to spend one day each on the park, the falls and the beach.
Taking a bus from Manila to Cabanatuan (Nueva Ecija) first takes about
3 hours
From the Cabanatuan terminal, a van to Baler costs about
(it varies by source) and takes about
3–4 hours
; it leaves once the seats are full.
Some sources say Genesis buses also run from the Cabanatuan Central Terminal at intervals of a few hours, but fares differ by source, so confirm locally.
Take the North Luzon Expressway (NLEX), exit at Santa Rita (Bulacan), head toward Cabanatuan, and at Bongabon turn right following the Baler sign; the road then leads up into the park.
The road is paved but winding, with steep grades and many narrow stretches. Slow down in fog and rain.
Flights from Manila to Baler have been described as small aircraft landing at San Luis airfield, but schedules change, so always check the latest information. The land route is the standard way.
There are no public transport stops or visitor shuttles inside the park. Ride a Baler–Cabanatuan van or bus through it, or stop along the way by rental car, motorbike or a local tour.

Because this is a mountain-road trip, the weather is the biggest variable. The dry season from November to May is safer and gives better visibility. In the rainy season from June to October, rain and fog make the road slippery and landslides are a risk.
Birdwatching is best in the early morning, and the scenery is especially lovely around sunrise or just after the rain clears. In any season, plan to leave the mountain section before dark.

blocks.label: Season at a glance
rows: Move mostly in the early morning, carry plenty of water

items.label: Park entrance fee
items.note: Some sources say there is no separate fee when only passing through, while others advise a permit and guide, so confirm with the DENR Aurora office (no official 2026 fee schedule found)

items.label: Ditumabo Falls entrance
items.note: Per person, per 2026 sources; vehicle parking about ₱30 extra, check the posted rate

items.label: Ditumabo guide
items.note: Per group of up to 10–12 people, per 2026 sources; a local guide is required under local rules

items.label: Meals, water and snacks
items.note: Almost no shops inside the park, so prepare in Baler

There is almost no lodging or dining inside the park. Most people stay in the beach town of Baler and visit as a day trip, or use lodging such as the Villa Aurora Ecotourism Area in Maria Aurora to the west. Baler is a surfing town, so it has a wide choice of guesthouses and restaurants.

Maria Aurora also has cafes and small eateries. Opening status can change, so check before you go, and carry your own water and snacks on the mountain road. Using local restaurants and small shops also helps the local economy.
Bring water, snacks, insect repellent, binoculars and a camera before you set out. There are said to be almost no shops inside the park.
Mobile signal is weak or drops out in many stretches. Download maps in advance and tell family or your accommodation your route.
After dark, fog and darkness make the road dangerous, so cross the mountain section during the daytime.
If you are driving, fill the tank before leaving and carry emergency supplies.
To see birds, move quietly along the roadside in the early morning.
Be quiet and respectful at the Aurora Quezon memorial marker and do not leave trash.

It is unclear whether an entrance fee or permit is required, so the most reliable way is to check ahead with the DENR or the Aurora provincial tourism office. You may be asked for a small environmental donation by the roadside, so carry small bills.
In the rainy season landslides, slippery roads and thick fog are frequent, so postpone your plans if rain is forecast.
The road is winding, steep and narrow in places. Slow down and sound your horn before blind curves.
There are no maintained trails, so do not go deep into the forest away from the road. If you want to head toward the summit, first check permits and guide requirements.
There are almost no restrooms or shops inside the park. Prepare what you need in advance.
Some websites list places here as closed, but the road and the protected area are open to the public. Confirm the latest operating status of individual facilities locally.
In mountain areas, weather and security conditions can change. Check the latest local notices.
A coastal town at the eastern end of the park road. It has attractions such as surfing, the town museum and the Aurora Quezon house, and most visitors stay here.
A waterfall in San Luis, about
20–40 minutes
by car from Baler. You walk about
1.3km
from the entrance and must be accompanied by a guide.
A large city in Nueva Ecija toward the western end of the park road. It serves as a transfer hub for travelers coming from Manila.
A coastal town on the southern side of Aurora province that can be visited as a separate trip. Public transport is limited, so check in advance.
